The externally exposed interfaces for KuzuDB and Postgres databases are standardized, allowing seamless switching between storage media. For graph data storage, the embedded graph database uses KuzuDB, while the online environment uses the Postgres Age plugin; both adopt a unified table structure: the Files node table stores basic information about each file in the codebase; the Functions node table stores information about functions defined in the code; the Contains relationship table represents the containment relationship between files and functions (Files → Functions); the FunctionCalls relationship table records call relationships between functions (Functions → Functions); the FileCalls relationship table records the direct invocation of functions by files (Files → Functions); the Imports relationship table represents import/export relationships between files (Files → Files); the Exports relationship table represents the relationship of files exporting functions (Files → Functions); the FunctionContains relationship table represents functions defining other functions internally (nested functions) (Functions → Functions). With the graph data tables described above, multi-level function dependencies can be queried to generate call-chain-like relationship graphs, providing the LLM with complete contextual information.
